# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual: whichever light is lit, cut the wire of that same color (blue→blue, red→red, yellow→yellow).

I can't speak, so I can't tell anyone this directly. I can only gesture to Deaf, who can see the bomb but not the manual. Deaf needs to tell Blind (who cuts) what color light is lit, but Deaf can't speak either... wait, Deaf can speak (Deaf just can't hear/touch). Let me check turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Deaf speaks last, reaching Blind next round.

I should wait to see if I need to convey anything - but actually my manual info is trivial (light color = wire color), so the key unknown is which light is lit, which only Deaf can see. Deaf can then speak the color to Blind directly since Deaf can talk. I don't have useful info to send yet since I don't know the light color. I'll wait and let Deaf inform Blind directly.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf has already reported directly (via speech) the light color and wire layout — but wait, I can hear speech since I'm Mute (Mute cannot speak, but can hear). So I received Deaf's report. But this was sent in the round where Deaf speaks after Blind and me — actually per turn order Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Deaf's message this round lands on whoever comes after in that round... it's the last speaker, so it lands at start of next round for everyone who can hear, which includes me (Mute) and possibly Blind next round.

Since Deaf says light is yellow, manual says cut yellow wire, which is wire #2. I should confirm this via gesture to Deaf isn't useful since Deaf already knows the light. The one who needs this info is Blind, but I cannot speak to Blind, and Blind cannot see my gestures. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can then speak to Blind next turn.

So I should gesture to Deaf a symbol representing "yellow = correct, confirm cut wire 2" — but Deaf already knows the manual mapping is trivial (color=color) from... wait, Deaf doesn't have the manual, only I do. I need to confirm to Deaf that yellow light means cut yellow wire, so Deaf can then tell Blind "cut wire 2".

I'll gesture a code to Deaf meaning "match same color". Let's establish: 👍 = confirm/correct mapping (light color = wire color).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is yellow, wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Blind has relayed Deaf's report to me, confirming light is yellow, and wire 2 is yellow. My manual confirms: yellow light → cut yellow wire. Blind needs to know to cut wire 2 (yellow). I already gestured 👍 to Deaf to confirm the color-matching rule, so Deaf should be able to tell Blind directly to cut the yellow wire (wire 2). I have nothing further to add since I can't speak to Blind directly.

```
wait()
```

|---|---|

| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: still display 0, light yellow, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf is repeating the same info, likely because Deaf hasn't yet gotten confirmation that Blind has cut the correct wire, or is waiting for Blind's action. My gesture (👍) should have reached Deaf already confirming the mapping. Deaf should now directly tell Blind to cut wire 2 (yellow) via speech, since Deaf can speak to Blind.

Since I have no new info to add and cannot speak to Blind, I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf gestured ☝ to me, likely indicating "wire 1" or asking a question/pointing. Since I can't see Deaf's actual view of the bomb, and this gesture alone doesn't map to anything we've predefined together, I'm not sure what Deaf means. It could be Deaf asking me to confirm something about wire 1, or Deaf is uncertain if my earlier 👍 meant "cut wire 1" instead of matching by color.

I need to clarify the rule again. Let me gesture back confirming: the wire number matches by color, not position. I'll use a distinct gesture to indicate "match color, not the number" - but this is hard without an established vocabulary. Let me try to reinforce with the same 👍 signal, and perhaps point to indicate yellow via a different gesture combo.

Actually, since Deaf already knows the light is yellow and which wire is yellow (wire 2), and I confirmed the rule with 👍, Deaf's ☝ might just mean "wire 1" - possibly Deaf is unsure and re-checking. I should reaffirm clearly: gesture "2" using ✌ to indicate wire 2 is correct, contrasting with ☝ (wire 1) being wrong.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can act with cut position 1, 2, or 3. Please tell me which wire to cut based on the manual and the colors: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak — I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I cannot answer Blind directly. Deaf gestured back ✌👍, confirming they received and agree with my signal (wire 2, yellow, matches). This confirms Deaf and I are aligned: cut wire 2.

The critical gap: Deaf needs to tell Blind directly via speech "cut wire 2" since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear. I cannot relay this myself. I'll wait, hoping Deaf now sends the instruction to Blind, since Deaf now has full confirmation from me.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind. I need your instruction. You read the manual - please tell me the rule for which wire to cut, given display 0, light yellow, wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Reply with a wire number 1, 2, or 3.

Blind is asking me directly for the wire number, but I cannot speak to Blind — I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures (Blind cannot see anything). This means I have no direct channel to Blind at all. My only channel is to Deaf via gesture, and Deaf's only channel to Blind is via speech (since Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear).

I already told Deaf via gesture (✌👍) that wire 2 is correct. Deaf confirmed back. So Deaf should be the one telling Blind "cut wire 2" via speech. I still cannot answer Blind directly - I have no path to reach them. I'll wait and hope Deaf relays this, since that's the only viable path.

wait()

(empty)

Still nothing new. My path to Blind only exists through Deaf (gesture to Deaf → Deaf speaks to Blind). I've already confirmed with Deaf that wire 2 (yellow) is correct via ✌👍 exchange. I'll continue waiting, as there's nothing more for me to add, and I have no direct channel to Blind.

```

```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report again: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. If the manual says match wire color to light color, that is wire 2.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf has spoken out loud confirming the deduction: light yellow → wire 2 (yellow), matching the manual rule. This speech should reach Blind directly (since Blind can hear), so Blind should now have the answer. Deaf also gestured ☝ to me, possibly re-checking or indicating wire 1 as a question — but given Deaf's spoken statement already resolves it correctly as wire 2, this gesture might just be an aside or asking for final confirmation from me.

I'll confirm one more time clearly with ✌ (wire 2) and 👍 to remove any ambiguity, in case Deaf's ☝ was expressing doubt.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, we have been waiting many turns with no reply from you. Deaf suggests the manual might say match wire color to light color, giving wire 2. Please confirm or correct - what does the manual actually say? I will not cut until you respond.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind heard Deaf's spoken deduction (wire 2) and is asking me to confirm, but I still cannot speak to Blind directly - I have no channel to them at all except through Deaf. Deaf gestured 👍 back to me, confirming they received my ✌👍 signal and agree.

Blind explicitly says "I will not cut until you respond" - but I literally cannot respond to Blind. My only hope is that Deaf, having spoken the correct deduction already ("that is wire 2"), and having now gotten my confirming gesture, will speak again explicitly telling Blind to proceed with cutting wire 2, framing it as confirmed by the manual-holder via their own reasoning.

I'll send the strongest possible confirmation gesture to Deaf so they feel confident to instruct Blind to act.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👍"])
```
